title: Context window, cost per token and practical limits

videos.script: A model call has a price and a size, and both are counted in tokens. {{tokens}} The size first. Every model has a window, and the question and the answer share it. Overfill it and, depending on who runs the model, the request is refused before anything is written, or quietly cut. {{window}} Then the price. You pay per million tokens, and output costs several times what input does. You read a real price list, with its date, and turn one request into the cost of a feature for a month. {{bill}} Then the two costs nobody puts in the first estimate. A conversation resends itself every turn, so its cost grows faster than its length. And the same long prompt, sent again and again, can be cached and paid for at a tenth. {{cache}} Last, the guard. A reply cut off at its limit, and a budget checked in code before the request leaves. {{guard}}
